sources: dossier=Net position 'Terminate semantics' + Required behaviors 'Force-terminate' + Conflicts 'RESOLVED 2026-07-14 (user ruling, transcript tier): active cancel confirmed... ruled in the finding-437 adjudication (2026-07-13) and re-ratified 2026-07-14'; doc=line 29 'any pending messages on the instance's queue are marked cancelled and never open a frame'; code=handleTerminateInstance never calls CancelPendingForInstance, pending messages stay cancelled=0 and are merely unpickable via the terminated_at filter
note: The dossier's own conflicts log already adjudicated this exact row: terminate must actively cancel pending messages, and the doc's 'marked cancelled' claim is the intended target state, not drift. The gap is in handleTerminateInstance, which never calls CancelPendingForInstance. Doc is correct as written; queue a code fix to call CancelPendingForInstance (and relax its terminated_at IS NULL guard) from force-terminate. Not editing the doc.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'Frame state lives entirely in run scopes and node_runs... nothing about frame execution or resolution changes the state of the instance row'; doc(before)=lines 33 and 35 both asserted 'frame processing never mutates the instance row / mutates only the message queue', restating the identical invariant twice
note: Both statements were correct restatements of the same rule (confirmed by dossier), so this was a doc-internal redundancy, not an intent conflict. Merged the two invariants into the single more-complete statement (the exhaustive-field-list version, formerly line 35) and deleted the redundant line 33.

sources: dossier=silent on table naming, but design corpus self-containment rule (.ok-planner/CLAUDE.md) forbids code-layer identities (table/file/package names) in concept body; doc(before)=line 33 named raw table `rimsky_instances` as the write target, which is also imprecise since the two legitimate writes hit rimsky_messages not rimsky_instances
note: Self-containment rule is a design-corpus-level constraint, not merely a style nit, and the finding's own imprecision point (writes target rimsky_messages, not rimsky_instances) is independently correct. Resolved as part of the 438 merge: the surviving invariant text talks about 'the instance row' and 'the message queue' generically, with no raw table identifier.

Rewrote line 25's closing clause to 'unused matchers surface via event-derived per-entry match counts, aggregated at read time from concept:event-log rather than persisted on the instance row', aligning with line 19's 'per-entry' framing and removing the false storage claim.
